title: Client-side error monitoring and crash reporting

videos.script:
A server that fails writes a line in its own log, on a machine you run. A page that fails does it in somebody's browser, on a phone you will never see, and tells nobody.

{{catch}} So the page has to tell you. Two listeners catch what the code did not: an error that escaped, and a promise nobody handled. And the planner's own catches report too, instead of writing to a console no one reads.

{{collector}} Reports go to a collector. Yours will be thirty lines of Node, which keeps each report on a line of its own and refuses anything too large to be one.

{{maps}} Then a bug, shipped on purpose, in a production build. Its stack trace points at line one, column five thousand and sixteen, of a minified file. Source maps turn that back into a line of main.ts, and you will keep those maps off the public host, where they would hand out your source.

{{release}} Every report names the build it came from, so a map can be found and a fix can be confirmed.

{{privacy}} And what a report must not carry. An error is data about a person, and the LGPD says what you owe them.
